correctness.rationale: In the complement, the selected graph is P4+(r-2)K2 on 2r vertices with r+1 edges and maximum degree 2. If a d-regular host complement has t other vertices, selected-to-outside incidence gives (2r-t)d<=2(r+1); as d>=2, t>=r-1. The cyclic host complement C_{3r-1} has an induced copy by blocks of lengths 4,2,...,2 separated by one vertex. All boundaries, including r=2, are handled; finite verifier ran on r=2..100.

value.rationale: The theorem quantifies a linear r-1 increase in the minimum induced Cayley-host order caused by removing only one edge from the natural vertex-transitive cocktail-party family. It extends a recently investigated embedding invariant, proves a stronger vertex-transitive lower bound, and has exact constructions for unbounded r. It is not a recomputation of small instances, and the known clique-coclique inequality alone gives only the weaker 2r floor.
